reading.body:
The dataset covers exactly one data center facility in Virginia, operated by Spanberger in Ashburn, with zero megawatts of capacity recorded.

That single record is the whole of the evidence here. One facility, one operator, one city, and a capacity figure of zero. The zero may mean the capacity is unknown, not yet built, or simply not tracked in this source, and the data does not say which. Nothing in the record establishes a trend, a comparison, or a share of anything.

What this does not tell the reader is nearly everything that matters for AI. There is no power draw, no grid interconnection, no construction date, no cost, and no indication of whether this facility serves AI workloads at all. A capacity of zero megawatts, if taken literally, would mean a building that consumes no power, which is not a useful fact about a data center.

The one thing the record does support is location. Ashburn is named, and Ashburn is where a large concentration of data center capacity sits. But this dataset contains a single facility, so it cannot show that concentration, measure it, or connect it to compute demand. Treat it as a placeholder entry, not as evidence about the grid or about AI scaling.
